quotes.text: When angry, count ten, before you speak; if very angry, an hundred.
quotes.author: Thomas Jefferson

source.work: Letter to Thomas Jefferson Smith, Monticello, enclosing 'A Decalogue of Canons for observation in practical life' (canon 10)
source.locator: The Writings of Thomas Jefferson, Memorial ed., vol. XVI (Washington, 1903–04), p. 111

quotes.verification_note: Added 2026-10-04 by the verifier under the owner's 'best genuine line per person' rule, replacing A16/A17, which have no fame evidence. Normalised match = True in the archive.org OCR of the Memorial edition vol. XVI (writingsofthomas0016unse), inside the letter to Thomas Jefferson Smith of 21 Feb 1825, after the heading 'A Decalogue of Canons…'; search-inside p. 111 (same page in jeffersonthomas16lipsrich). US public domain; Jefferson wrote in English.
quotes.fame_evidence: Bartlett's Familiar Quotations, 18th ed. (2012) p. 338 and 17th ed. (2002) p. 359, Jefferson entry (snippet has 'Decalogue', 'angry', 'hundred'), checked by archive.org search-inside. The most-anthologised Jefferson line that fits the app's themes; his other anthology lines are political.
